summary: Ep 13's mixed typing was ruled on an estimate; wave 3 measured it with two timestamped subtitle files and the ruling STANDS. Of the episode's 20m20s of story time, Arakawa's tankōbon extras occupy 690.3s = 56.6% (the two gaiden 647.3s = 53.0%, the four-panel omake 43.0s = 3.5%) and 2003-original material 530.2s = 8m50s = 43.4%, in nine blocks across the whole run of the episode. That original share is story-carrying on three independent readings: its size; the licensor's own synopsis, which is the original thread end to end and never mentions the dog, the cat or the festival; and its load — the Marcoh thread, Grand, the Führer's entourage and Douglas, Hughes' promotion, the Reole reversal and the alchemist killings are what eps 14-15 run on. The verdict is robust to every boundary judgment I had to make: the source share lands between 47.8% and 56.6% under the most generous reading in either direction, so neither canon nor filler survives. Two note repairs replace the wave-2 estimates with the measured figures, and one repair removes a beat the stored side_story note credits to the episode that is NOT in it (the Military Festival's coda — Hughes drinking coffee through the cleanup, found by Armstrong — is cut, and Armstrong does not appear in ep 13 at all); a new `abridged` record carries that. No anchor: the three extras are unnumbered, so the row stays A44 position-less, and nothing in the series' position map moves. AFG has no 2003 FMA page at all — the minute-range instrument the ask offered does not exist for this series, which is why the subtitle files had to be the instrument.

anchor_hostile.why: A44 — position-less by chapter space. Everything ep 13 adapts is an UNNUMBERED tankōbon extra: 'The Military Festival' (vol 3 back matter, 11 pp, printed after ch 12), 'Dog of the Military?' (vol 4 back matter, 11 pp, printed after ch 16) and the four-panel omake 'The Ambitious Alchemist'. en-WP's chapter list prints them as bare `Gaiden.` rows with no number; fma.fandom's Chapter Infobox leaves `chapter number` empty on both; MangaDex's 12.5 / 16.5 sort keys are scanlator placements, not printed numbers (N35). There is no chapter number to anchor on, and the row must not borrow ch 12 or ch 16 — those are adapted elsewhere. Unchanged from the wave-2 finding; the wave-3 sizing does not create a position.

annotations.chapters: FMA bonus chapter: 'The Military Festival' (軍部の祭り, unnumbered gaiden, tankōbon vol 3 back matter) — its closing pages
annotations.note: The gaiden's CODA IS CUT. In 'The Military Festival', after Bradley orders every soldier present to help repair the wrecked parade grounds, Havoc notices Hughes is missing; Major Alex Louis Armstrong finds Maes in the break room drinking coffee, and Hughes answers with his own idiom — 'a soldier should know when to retreat.' That is the chapter's punchline and its last beat. It is NOT in ep 13: the episode's cleanup runs 18:02.0-18:15.5 (13.5s) and ends on Hawkeye's line that the two of them have been ordered to fix it and on the transmutation itself, then cuts straight to Ed asking why Mustang held back. Armstrong has no line and no appearance anywhere in the episode — he is absent from all 398 Japanese cues, from all 353 English cues, and from fma.fandom's full synopsis. The stored side_story note credits the coda to the episode; it does not belong there (see the repair). weight: n/a — this is an OMISSION of source material, recorded so the census can see that the vol-3 gaiden is adapted in substance but not in full; it does not change the standing (T28's faithfulness clause: cuts and omissions of the source's own events are annotations, never a type). The other adaptation-side alterations (the wager premise, the draw) are already carried by the stored `divergence` record.

repairs.old: A NEW record: the stored row carried no annotation at all, so nothing said WHAT ep 13 adapts — and the ep-37 record's claim that ep 13 rests on 'the same basis' as ep 37 is wrong twice over (different extras, and ep 37 also carries a novel segment ep 13 has none of). fma.fandom's Episode 13 notes: 'This episode is adapted from the material of the manga bonus chapters Dog of the Military? and The Military Festival'; both gaiden pages say the same from the other direction ('The events of this Bonus Chapter would be adapted into parts of Episode 13: Fullmetal vs. Flame'), and SlashFilm's 2024-12-15 piece on the episode independently reports the same pair plus the omake ('to expand the runtime, the episode incorporates two other bonus chapters: Dog of the Military… and a non-canonical four-panel omake titled The Ambitious Alchemist'), with the fandom's Volume 4 page listing 'The Ambitious Alchemist: Part 2' among that volume's omake. WHAT IS IN THE EPISODE, PIECE BY PIECE. From 'The Military Festival': the argument over who would win, Ed being in East City for his annual State Alchemist assessment, Hughes brokering the parade grounds, Bradley approving the match, the crowd, Ed's coat decoy, the destroyed ignition glove and Mustang's second glove up the other sleeve, the Führer ordering everyone to clean up the wrecked grounds, Hughes drinking coffee through it ('a soldier should know when to retreat'). From 'Dog of the Military?': Fuery's rain-soaked puppy, Breda's terror of dogs, Havoc's stir-fry joke, the Elrics refusing because they travel, Al hiding a cat in his armour and running off crying, Mustang's 'faithful servants' line, Hawkeye taking the dog and firing a ring of shots around it for wetting the floor (the anime even reproduces the chapter's own art error — seven holes for six shots). From the omake: Mustang's declaration that as Führer he would put every female officer in a miniskirt. weight: SIGNIFICANT for the two gaiden — they are 11 pages each (MangaDex's page counts, against 32-52 pages for a numbered chapter) and they carry the episode's title fight and its running B-plot, roughly 10-12 minutes of a ~23-minute episode; weight: SLIVER for the four-panel omake — a single gag scene, no story weight, noted so it stays visible. None of the three is adapted in any other episode of the run. DIRECTION IS CLEAN: vol 3 shipped 2002-09-21 and vol 4 2003-01-22, both a year or more before this episode aired on 2003-12-27 (the GTO/souleater trap does not apply).

(1) 'roughly 10-12 minutes of a ~23-minute episode' was the author's estimate, which the wave-2 verifier flagged as unsourced; it is replaced by the measured figures and the full timed segment table (two timestamped subtitle files; the two gaiden 10m47s = 53.0% of 20m20s of story time, the omake 43s = 3.5%). The estimate was accurate — this is a sourcing repair, not a correction. (2) A FACTUAL correction: the note lists 'Hughes drinking coffee through it (a soldier should know when to retreat)' among what the episode takes from 'The Military Festival'. The clause is replaced by an explicit statement that the coda is cut, pointing at the new `abridged` record.

repairs.old: THE 2003-ORIGINAL HALF OF EP 13 — the record the row lacked, and the basis for the mixed typing. (a) THE PREMISE IS REPLACED. In the gaiden the exhibition match happens because a barracks argument about who is stronger gets out of hand; in the anime Ed proposes it as a WAGER — if he wins, Mustang tells him about the travelling alchemist doctor — a thread that exists only because eps 11-12 adapted the novel's Xenotime story (Belsio's tip). The licensor's own synopsis of the episode is that thread, not the duel: 国家錬金術師としての調査報告のために、軍・東方司令部を訪れたエドとアル。エドはゼノタイムで聞いたドクター・マルコーの噂を、マスタング大佐に尋ねてみるが軽くかわされてしまう。そこでエドは一計を案じ… (b) THE OUTCOME IS REPLACED. The gaiden ends 'with a huge, final blast, Edward is soundly defeated'; the anime ends in a DRAW because Mustang freezes on an Ishbal flashback, which is then the hook for Mustang's tip and for eps 14-15. (c) ADDED ORIGINAL PLOT, none of it in any extra: the Reole debrief; Brigadier General Grand arriving with the Führer's entourage to make Eastern Command a temporary HQ; the Führer's secretary Juliet Douglas (Sloth) whom Ed eyes with suspicion — the 2003 series planting its own endgame; Grand branding Marcoh a deserter and traitor; Hughes' promotion to Lt. Colonel and head of Investigations; Ed's failed search of the archives; and the closing Hughes/Mustang bar scene (Reole is still in strife under Hakuro, Mustang decides to keep it from Ed, Scar is confirmed to be moving on East City). Roughly half the runtime, and it is the material eps 14-15 run on. Under T28's faithfulness clause (a) and (b) alone would be divergence on a canon row; it is (c) — a story-carrying original share — that makes the row mixed.

Colonel and head of Investigations, Grand branding Marcoh a deserter (93.4s); 10:18.9-10:32.1 the archive search, the records erased (13.2s); 15:13-15:26 Ed's terms — Marcoh's file and the cat (13.0s); 18:15.5-19:49 'why did you hold back?', the Ishbal flashback, Marcoh 'was the sanest of us', 'you should meet him' (93.5s); 20:28.4-21:10 the Hughes/Mustang bar scene, Reole in civil war under Hakuro, Mustang deciding to keep it from Ed (41.6s); 21:37-22:23 'this is no inspection', five State Alchemists killed in Central, Scar's kill and 'East City' (46.0s). THE T28 TEST. The original share is not connective framing, on three independent readings. (i) SIZE: 8m50s, 43.4% of the story time, in nine blocks spread across the whole episode, the largest of them 116s. (ii) THE LICENSOR CALLS IT THE PLOT: Bandai Channel's own synopsis of 第13話 is the original thread end to end and never mentions the dog, the cat or the festival — 国家錬金術師としての調査報告のために、軍・東方司令部を訪れたエドとアル。エドはゼノタイムで聞いたドクターマルコーの噂を、マスタング大佐に尋ねてみるが軽くかわされてしまう。そこでエドは一計を案じ、マルコーの情報を賭け、マスタング大佐と模擬戦闘を行なうことに…… — i.e. the duel is the INSTRUMENT of the original A-plot, not the episode's job. fma.fandom's own one-line synopsis reads the same way ('If Ed wins, Roy must tell the truth about the traveling doctor who saved children in Xenotime'). (iii) IT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR LATER ROWS: the Marcoh thread opened here (Grand branding him a deserter, the erased records, Mustang's Ishbal hesitation and his tip) is what eps 14-15 run on; Grand and the Führer's entourage, Hughes' promotion, the Douglas glance, the Reole-is-still-burning reversal and the five dead State Alchemists are all first plantings of the 2003 series' own line — the wiki's own episode note says exactly that ('utter proof enough that the staff of the 2003 anime were pretty much building up an original story all around from the very beginning'). SOURCE + ANIME-ORIGINAL IN ONE EPISODE, both story-carrying = mixed (T27/T28). ROBUST IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — the typing does not hang on any boundary judgment. Count the omake as original and the split is source 53.0% / original 47.0%. Push the other way and reassign the three most arguable source blocks (the assessment announcement 33.0s, the who-would-win debate 47.2s, the cat's doorstep closure 27.0s — each a gaiden beat the anime restages inside its own frame) to the original side, and the split is source 47.8% / original 52.2%. Every reading lands between 47% and 57% source: neither 'the extras carry the episode' (which would make it canon with the changes as divergence) nor 'the extras are a fragment' (which would make it filler with a graft) survives the numbers. NOT CANON, therefore, under T28's faithfulness clause: the replaced premise (a wager for Marcoh's file, not a barracks argument) and the replaced outcome (a draw from Mustang's Ishbal freeze, not the gaiden's decisive final blast) would indeed be mere divergence on a canon row — but they sit on top of 8m50s of plot that is in no extra at all. NOT FILLER: a weight-bearing side_story tie of 11m30s. THE INSTRUMENTS, AND THEIR PRECISION. (1) A timestamped Japanese subtitle file for this exact episode — kitsunekko's `Fullmetal Alchemist (01-51).zip`, file `Fullmetal Alchemist.S01E13.JA.srt`, a rip of the Netflix Japanese closed captions: 398 cues with millisecond in/out timecodes, running 00:00:13.346 to 00:23:50.053, and its cue 396 names the NEXT episode 「第14話『破壊の右手』」 — which is our stored ep-14 title, so the file is keyed to our row, not to an index. (2) A second, independently produced and independently timed file from a DIFFERENT release lineage — kitsunekko's English `Fullmetal Alchemist TV Episode 01-51 ENG.zip`, file `fma13.srt`, a fansub timed to the TV broadcast (353 cues, it also translates the on-screen East City sign at 00:00:09 and the OP/ED lyrics, which the Netflix CC track does not — proof it is not a re-time of the same text). PRECISION: cue times are exact to the millisecond; a SCENE boundary is placed at the mid-point of the silent gap between the last cue of one scene and the first cue of the next, so each boundary is good to about ±2s and each segment duration to about ±3s. AGREEMENT: the same 26 blocks measured independently in both files differ by at most 4.5s (the OP and the office dog scene) and by 2s or less on 20 of the 26; the duel measures 156.0s in both. The ratio therefore does not depend on the file chosen. WHAT WAS NOT AVAILABLE: animefillerguide has NO 2003 Fullmetal Alchemist page at all — its search returns only 'Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood', and /anime/fullmetal-alchemist/ SERVES the Brotherhood page (title 'Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood Filler List and Order to Watch'), so the AFG minute-range instrument the ask offered as an option does not exist for this series; animefillerlist carries no timings, only 'Manga Canon' on this row.

structure.instrument: A timestamped subtitle file is a real T28 sizing instrument and it is available for far more series than AFG's minute ranges. kitsunekko.net carries per-episode files in BOTH directions — `dirlist.php?dir=subtitles%2Fjapanese%2F<series>%2F` (Japanese, largely Netflix/Amazon CC rips) and `dirlist.php?dir=subtitles%2F<series>%2F` (English fansubs) — and for Fullmetal Alchemist both hold a complete 01-51 archive, so two independently timed files of the same episode were available. Downloads need a Referer header set to the directory page. The identity check that makes such a file safe to use: FMA's next-episode preview is subtitled, so cue 396 of the ep-13 file names 「第14話『破壊の右手』」 — the file is bound to our row by title, not by index (R20).
structure.afg_negative: animefillerguide has NO Fullmetal Alchemist (2003) page. Its search (?s=fullmetal) returns only Brotherhood, and the plausible slug /anime/fullmetal-alchemist/ RETURNS 200 while serving the Brotherhood page (<title>Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood Filler List and Order to Watch</title>) — a G55-shaped namesake trap: a 200 is not a page. The AFG minute-range option in the ask is unavailable for this series.
structure.unresolved_omake_placement: Which volume carries the miniskirt line is STILL unverified, exactly as the wave-2 verifier left it. fma.fandom's Volume 3 omake list has 'The Ambitious Alchemist'; its Volume 4 list has 'The Ambitious Alchemist: Part 2' (alongside 'Cat' and 'Cat: Episode 2', which are not claimed by any source as ep-13 material). No printed TOC, Bookwalker listing or ja-WP page names either part's content, and a fandom search for 'miniskirt' returns pages with empty snippets.
